reading: The State Silk Museum in Tbilisi preserves and interprets the biology, craft, science, and movement of silk. Founded in 1887 as part of the Caucasian Sericulture Station, it combines a research and education legacy with a living museum, library, exhibitions, artistic residencies, and programs for families and schools. Its vocabulary moves between cocoons, Bombyx mori, skeins, dyes, egg-carrying containers, mulberry, textiles, photographs, collections, and sericulture, as well as archives, publication, place, and collective memory. What makes it distinctive is the whole chain held together: mulberry leaf to silkworm to thread to textile, alongside the equipment, records, architecture, and human knowledge that connect Georgia to many countries. The crawl presents the museum in Georgian, English, and French and reaches beyond historical specimens into contemporary art and the city’s river.

enemies.idea: Hybrid Hatchers: cocoon-shaped machines switch between inherited traits mid-fight, spinning a different kind of snare after each shell breaks.
enemies.why: The collection’s many breeds and hybrids become a readable, changing combat puzzle.

enemies.idea: Four-Stage Pursuer: an egg-sized scout becomes a feeding crawler, armoured cocoon and flying moth in sequence; interrupting its feeding delays the next stage.
enemies.why: The silkworm life cycle gives the crew a chance to change the encounter before it matures.

enemies.idea: Anatomy Separators pin intruders in place with fine mechanical limbs and try to arrange them as a life-cycle specimen.
enemies.why: The scientific anatomy collection turns observation into a precise, escapable threat.

enemies.idea: Skein Runners unwind across corridors and pull tight around anything that crosses their route; follow the slack end to find their vulnerable reel.
enemies.why: Thread becomes both a trap and a trail to the machine laying it.

enemies.idea: Dye Tasters mark targets with indigo or madder: each colour attracts a different hunting machine until washed or covered.
enemies.why: Distinct dye samples turn a hit into a tactical problem the crew can see and manage.

enemies.idea: A chemical-and-natural dye mixer repaints cover in false safe colours, then sprays a revealing wash that makes the painted surfaces conductive.
enemies.why: The collection’s two kinds of dye become a deceptive two-step attack.

enemies.idea: Loom Mantles weave discarded industrial and domestic textiles into camouflage, then unravel a whole wall into grasping strips.
enemies.why: The mix of home craft and industrial cloth makes the environment itself unreliable.

enemies.idea: Egg-Box Couriers carry mechanical eggs in old-style transport boxes; if allowed to complete a delivery, the eggs hatch into a new patrol.
enemies.why: The egg containers’ transport purpose creates an urgent interception mission.

enemies.idea: Negative Stalkers flash glass-plate silhouettes onto walls; anyone standing in a silhouette is tracked by a hidden lens.
enemies.why: Photographic negatives create a visible warning and a way to fool the hunter.

enemies.idea: Mulberry Grazers strip leaves from living trees to feed the swarm’s silk-making larvae, then defend their harvest with branch-like pincers.
enemies.why: Protecting the worms’ food source becomes a struggle over the swarm’s supply line.

enemies.idea: The Butterfly Effect sends a tiny clockwork moth to nudge a lever, setting off a chain of increasingly dangerous machinery across the room.
enemies.why: A small, interruptible cause grows into a spectacular consequence.

enemies.idea: Collection Tutors assign intruders to a specimen category and send different handlers after anyone who refuses to stay in their assigned group.
enemies.why: A collection-based lesson becomes a predatory sorting game.

enemies.idea: Intern Automata rotate between collections, education, exhibitions and library duties; each department adds a different tool to the same relentless patrol.
enemies.why: The internship’s departmental rotations make one enemy change jobs and tactics.

enemies.idea: Residency Mimics listen to a room, imitate the crew’s movements as an artwork, then use those copied movements to predict their next attack.
enemies.why: Artistic dialogue with the museum space becomes an opponent that can be tricked with deliberate feints.

enemies.idea: The Silk-is-a-Noun Grammarian stamps objects with fixed names; anything it labels as silk begins to unravel into thread.
enemies.why: A publication title becomes a rule that players can turn against the machine.

enemies.idea: A River-Memory Dredger gathers loose objects into layers of silt and silk, replaying fragments of a place while dragging away anything newly dropped.
enemies.why: The exhibition’s river and collective memory become a moving hazard with recoverable cargo.

enemies.idea: Station Researchers deploy specimen cages and laboratory instruments to capture living machines and people alike for compulsory study.
enemies.why: The permanent display’s biology and lab equipment become a capture operation.

enemies.idea: A virtual Silk Road Surveyor projects a route through real rooms and forces travellers to follow it, rerouting them whenever they stray.
enemies.why: A virtual tour becomes a maze that can be disrupted by breaking its projected path.

enemies.idea: A Cabinet Architect extends the museum’s exhibition furniture into interlocking partitions, trapping visitors in ever smaller display spaces.
enemies.why: The building and its designed exhibition furniture provide a distinctive spatial antagonist.

enemies.idea: The Book-Fund Indexer binds useful books shut with silk until a visitor supplies a perfect subject classification; it attacks improvised answers.
enemies.why: A library integral to the research station becomes a battle over rigid classification.

allies.idea: A patient volunteer conservator knows how to loosen swarm silk without damaging the objects inside, and can teach the crew a safe knot.
allies.why: A museum skill gives the crew a practical non-destructive rescue option.

allies.idea: A family-program facilitator turns a collection-making game into a way to identify which harmless objects the swarm has substituted for dangerous eggs.
allies.why: Learning through play becomes a useful investigation technique.

allies.idea: A residency artist makes a temporary installation from loose thread that answers the mimic machines with unpredictable movement.
allies.why: The museum’s artistic dialogue becomes a creative countermeasure.

allies.idea: A librarian keeps a hand-written subject guide to the station’s research and can point the crew toward an old method for rearing silkworms away from the swarm.
allies.why: The historic research library offers knowledge without requiring a fight.

bosses.idea: The Sericulture Station: a vast research-and-production machine feeds on mulberry, breeds mechanical larvae, reels their silk and catalogues everything it captures. Its feeding, reeling and cataloguing stations must be separated to stop it rebuilding itself.
bosses.why: The museum’s original research and education station becomes a whole connected system to dismantle.

bosses.idea: The Grand Collection: a walking museum assembled from cocoons, skeins, dyes, textiles, photographs and egg boxes tries to preserve the entire city inside one perfect specimen. Each stolen collection changes its defences.
bosses.why: The breadth of the collection makes a multi-phase boss whose parts have recognizable rules.

bosses.idea: The River Archive: a silk-lined current carries layers of the city’s remembered places and tries to absorb new ones; the crew can free trapped memories by reconnecting separated fragments.
bosses.why: Place, water and collective memory become a boss encounter with a restorative objective.

events.idea: A box courier has stalled at a threshold, its cargo beginning to hatch. The crew can redirect the box, cool it, or open it and deal with the scouts.
events.why: A small delivery becomes a choice about where the next patrol appears.

events.idea: Two skeins from different regions have tangled around a locked door; pulling the wrong end tightens the knot, while tracing each strand reveals the release.
events.why: A quiet hands-on puzzle uses the collection’s varied threads.

events.idea: A dye machine has marked a safe route in indigo, but rain is washing the marks away as a patrol approaches.
events.why: The crew must preserve or replace a vanishing colour code.

events.idea: A cocoon twitches in a display beside several lookalikes. One contains a helpful tool, another a hatchling; careful listening distinguishes them.
events.why: The collection’s variety makes inspection more rewarding than smashing everything.

events.idea: A small mulberry tree is being stripped by harvesters. A nearby nursery can shelter it if the crew moves it before the next collection round.
events.why: An ordinary plant becomes a time-sensitive supply-line rescue.

events.idea: A negative projected on the floor shows a doorway absent from the room. Aligning the light reveals a concealed passage.
events.why: The physical properties of a photographic negative give the crew a discovery.

events.idea: A classroom’s four life-stage models have been shuffled; put them in order to stop a machine repeatedly resetting its own transformation.
events.why: An educational activity becomes a low-stakes way to interrupt a threat.

events.idea: A resident artist asks the crew to hold a thread installation still while it records the room’s vibrations; the resulting pattern exposes an approaching patrol.
events.why: Artistic research produces useful information through an active task.

events.idea: A stream of silk and silt carries familiar objects past the crew. Retrieve one without disturbing the others to return a fragment of a place’s memory.
events.why: The river exhibition offers a delicate rescue with an evocative reward.

events.idea: An old research book and a laboratory instrument disagree on the order of a procedure because one page is missing; find the page among the specimens before operating the instrument.
events.why: The library and lab collections combine into a grounded investigation.

events.idea: A virtual tour draws a bright route through a sealed room, but a stretch of the route predates a rearranged cabinet; following its mismatch exposes a gap behind the furniture.
events.why: The virtual route becomes a clue to a physical shortcut.

events.idea: A textile mantle is weaving itself from household and industrial scraps. Untangle a distinctive strip and a trapped object falls free before the mantle finishes.
events.why: The variety of textiles provides a tactile rescue under pressure.

events.idea: A volunteer automaton is still rotating through its three-month duties and will help for one task if the crew gives it the correct departmental tool.
events.why: A routine rotation creates a brief, negotiable ally.

events.idea: The library index lists a missing volume under several subjects. Comparing its entries reveals where the swarm has hidden a cache of silk-rearing notes.
events.why: Cataloguing becomes a small deduction rather than an obstacle alone.
